comparator.name: Bachelor Applied Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh current 2026–2027 Mathematics and Computer Science after-revision PER, Articles 3.3–3.5 and Appendix 2 Applied Mathematics table p.78, establishes the ordinary English full-time single-degree curriculum. Twenty-eight credited positions total 60 + 60 + 60 = 180: core 125 including ordinary 2MBB10 Bachelor Final Project exactly 10, ITEC 10 and genuine open electives 45 (15 in year two, 30 in year three). Current Calculus for Applied Mathematics 2MCALCAM replaces 2WCB0 for September-2026 entrants under Appendix 3 p.90; no extra calculus is added. No formal specialization is required; select the broad ordinary pathway independently of UCR fit. Article 3.4 permits an alternative interdisciplinary Innovation Space final project of 15 EC by derogation; this is an optional alternative, not an extra requirement or a generic 10/15/20 range. The ordinary 10-credit final project spans two quarter positions and counts once. SCOP/e 2PRV21/2PRV22 and PPD are embedded; core CBL subparts add no credits. MyFuture requires value seven with no EC; at least five Studium Generale activities are part of ITEC requirements. Open electives require examination-board approval, no substantive overlap and at least 30 EC at levels 2/3 including 15 at level 3. BEP entry requires at least 120 credits including all compulsory first-year units; the 95-BCS-credit rule belongs to Computer Science, not Applied Mathematics. Multidisciplinary CBL requires completion of offered PPD-containing components. Detailed course assessment conditions and future timetabling remain applicable catalogue conditions. No new UCR judgment is made.

core: Calculus, linear algebra, probability, numerical methods and system models
Statistics, data analysis, stochastic modelling and empirical prediction
Programming, algorithms, optimisation and scientific computation
adjacent: Mathematical models of physical, industrial and sustainable systems

alternatives.label: Applied mathematics, algorithms & stochastic data models
alternatives.concept: Develop calculus, linear algebra, numerical methods, probability and linear systems through programming, algorithms, optimisation, statistical learning, image analysis, robotics and empirical stochastic models. This is the strongest applied computational response; proof-heavy analysis and algebra remain explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: Nineteen mathematical/computational courses plus four concrete statistical and decision-model applications support the label without claiming the external programme’s proof-intensive mathematical depth.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in year one and nine advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Programming precedes algorithms and autonomous decisions; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks. Research Methods & Statistics precedes Econometrics, while Probability & Statistics and Statistics & Experimental Methods precede the final empirical modelling work.

alternatives.label: Applied mathematics, computational systems & sustainable technology
alternatives.concept: Retain mathematical and computational system modelling while applying it to climate, renewable-energy and sustainability problems through scientific foundations, technical/economic energy assessment and autonomous technology.
alternatives.labelReason: Four sustainability/energy courses replace four statistics/economics applications and create a distinct physical-system and technology application strand.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, PPD in year one and nine advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Programming and Mathematical Methods precede their dependent advanced courses. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II, which precedes Renewable System Design; Climate Change supplies the later mitigation context.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses / 30 EC differ in each direction. Introductory economics, research methods, advanced human-data statistics and econometrics are replaced by two sustainability-science foundations, climate change and renewable-system design. These changes implement the evidenced physical/industrial-system application direction.

candidates.label: Mathematical modelling of physical, industrial and sustainable systems
Proof-intensive analysis, algebra and mathematical structures

selection.assessment: Two complete related-fields programmes pass the academic, 30-EC distinctness and feasibility gates. The first integrates numerical, stochastic, algorithmic and data-analysis interests; the second creates a materially different physical/sustainable-system application. A third proof-intensive direction cannot supply cumulative real analysis, measure/probability theory, algebraic structures, number theory, transforms, rigorous proof seminars or a mathematics research project. Logic, linear algebra and applied algorithms contribute foundations but are not relabelled as that specialist sequence.

blocks: Both develop formal logic and mathematical language; UCR emphasises discrete structures and algorithm construction.
Both establish calculus for applied mathematical models; UCR also introduces matrices and differential equations.
Both directly study linear algebra; the external second linear-algebra component remains separate additional depth.
Both directly develop numerical methods and error/stability reasoning.
Both address differential equations; UCR combines them with multivariable and complex calculus rather than the same ODE theory sequence.
Both establish probability and modelling; UCR integrates mathematical statistics and simulation.
Both use regression models for empirical prediction; econometrics specialises them to economic relationships.
Both provide statistical inference; UCR applies advanced models to human data rather than the same theoretical statistics syllabus.
Both use programming to construct mathematical models; UCR provides broader computer-science foundations.
Specialist mathematical depth, project and open profile

notes.text: The UCR programmes provide substantial calculus, linear algebra, probability, numerical methods, system models, programming, algorithms, optimisation and data analysis. They do not reproduce the target’s cumulative real analysis, advanced linear algebra, algebraic structures, graph theory, number theory, stochastic-process, measure-theory, transforms, proof or Applied Mathematics research-project depth.
